methods.label: Cancel consecutive factors
methods.explanation:
Subtracting each unit fraction from \(1\) gives a numerator one less than its denominator. For example, \(1-\frac13=\frac23\). Thus the nine factors become
\[
\frac12\cdot\frac23\cdot\frac34\cdots\frac9{10}
=\frac{1\cdot2\cdots9}{2\cdot3\cdots10}.
\]
Every integer from \(2\) through \(9\) appears once in both the numerator and denominator. Canceling these nonzero factors leaves \(\frac1{10}\), choice \(\mathrm{A}\).
